title: 2017 AMC 12B Problem 2
statement:
Real numbers \(x,\) \(y,\) and \(z\) satisfy the inequalities

\[0 \lt x \lt 1, \quad -1 \lt y \lt 0,\] and \[1 \lt z \lt 2.\]

Which of the following numbers is necessarily positive?

solutions.text:
Adding \(y \gt -1\) and \(z \gt 1\) gives \(y + z \gt 0,\) so \(y + z\) is always positive. Each of the other four choices can be made negative: with \(x = \tfrac18,\) \(y = -\tfrac14,\) \(z = \tfrac32,\) every one of \(y + x^2,\) \(y + xz,\) \(y + y^2,\) and \(y + 2y^2\) is negative.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Since \(y \gt -1\) and \(z \gt 1,\) what can you say about \(y + z?\)
For the other four, try \(x = \tfrac18,\) \(y = -\tfrac14,\) \(z = \tfrac32\) to force a negative value
